findings.issue_text: header.scss, topic-post.scss, and badges.css.scss use @include flexbox()/align-items/order mixins without importing common/foundation/mixins, which would break the Sass build at asset-compile time

Flexbox ordering via order(3) and margin-left: auto fails on -moz-box (Gecko never supported -moz-box-ordinal-group), causing .panel to render left-aligned and header controls to wrap or overlap the title
mixins.scss:120 declares display: -moz-inline-box, a fabricated property value never implemented by Gecko, misleading readers into thinking Firefox 2009 inline flex is covered
header.scss keeps .valign-helper after .contents became a flex container, leaving a dead-but-styled helper that can shift title vertical alignment and is a hazard for future layout edits

Flexbox conversion of .contents leaves out-of-diff float/position/width overrides in sibling stylesheets (responsive/mobile rules, plugin/theme overrides) dead or conflicting, breaking mobile/narrow-width header stacking

margin-left: auto push-right technique in the flex mixins fails on 2009 box-model browsers (-webkit-box/-moz-box/-ms-flexbox targets like iOS ≤6, Safari 5, old Android), collapsing the right-aligned header layout
Flex conversion of .small-action drops avatar/text spacing with no gap replacement, causing avatar and description text to butt against each other
Flex conversion of .small-action removes the 4em left padding, misaligning avatar-less small-action variants flush-left with surrounding posts
-ms-align-items is a nonexistent property (IE10 uses -ms-flex-align), emitting dead declarations and indicating the prefix matrix was never verified

Scope drift: unrelated redesign of .small-action visual styling in topic-post.scss:261-305, rewriting padding/margin scheme of .small-action-desc and zeroing p margins with no connection to header layout performance
Silent behavioral change masked as refactor: loss of the 4em avatar gutter in .small-action-desc (padding-left: 4em removed) changes rendered position of every small-action description

header.scss:36-39: @include order(3) on .panel plus order(2) on .extra-info-wrapper is a visual reordering feature, not performance optimization, and breaks DOM order = visual order including tab/focus order

mixins.scss:96-131: dead/incorrect legacy prefixes shipped in the diff, including invalid -ms-align-items (never in any spec) and -webkit-box-align/-webkit-box-ordinal-group with modern keyword values invalid under the 2009 box spec
mixins.scss ~118: dead vendor line `-ms-align-items` is not a valid property; old IE syntax is `-ms-flex-align`, so the declaration is silently discarded and provides no IE coverage

mixins.scss align-items/order mixins pass modern flexbox values verbatim into 2009-spec properties without value translation (e.g. flex-start is invalid for -webkit-box-align/-ms-flex-align), causing silent layout breakage in legacy browsers
order mixins: -ms-flex-order/-webkit-box-ordinal-group require integers and default to 1 instead of 0, causing reordering to differ across old/new spec boundaries
topic.scss:30 / header.scss:~40: visual reordering via order(2)/order(3) diverges from DOM order, breaking keyboard focus and tab order (WCAG 1.3.2 / 2.4.3 violation)

Silent visual redesign of .small-action in topic-post.scss:277-291 — padding/margin changes alter spacing of all small-action blocks unrelated to PR's stated header performance objective; the 1.5% width-dependent padding is a new visual decision rather than mechanical flex conversion

topic.scss:27-33 — deletion of &.bullet { margin-top: 5px } and addition of line-height: 1.5 to .extra-info-wrapper are unverified visual changes that shift category bullet badges vertically on every instance

mixins.scss:117 — align-items mixin emits nonexistent -ms-align-items property, producing dead declarations in every compiled stylesheet using it and misleading future maintainers debugging legacy flex alignment
align-items mixin family is internally inconsistent: -moz-box equivalent for align-items is missing while -moz-box-ordinal-group is included in order()

PR description mismatch: the diff is a layout-mechanism rewrite with visual re-spacing, not the stated performance optimization, so commit history records a false reason for user-visible changes and will mislead regression bisecting

The `order` mixin omits `-moz-box-ordinal-group`, so header panel reordering silently does nothing on old-Firebox flexbox engine the mixin targets, causing the panel to sit adjacent to the title instead of right-aligned

The mixin is internally inconsistent: it emits `-moz-box` compat lines for Firefox 18-21 but `order()` doesn't support that engine — either the compat targets are real (and broken) or the dead `-moz-box` lines should be deleted
The `-ms-align-items` declaration in `align-items()` is not a real property (IE10 uses `-ms-flex-align`), making it a redundant dead declaration

goldens.comment: Mixing float: left with flexbox causes layout issues. Further this PR removes the float-based right alignment for .d-header .panel, which may cause the login panel in the non-Ember/noscript header (where .panel is nested inside .row and not a flex item) to stack under the title instead of remaining right-aligned.
-ms-align-items never existed in any version of IE/Edge; the correct legacy property is -ms-flex-align.
-webkit-box-ordinal-group and -moz-box-ordinal-group require values starting from 1, not 0. If $val is 0, this will cause incorrect rendering in older browsers, leading to layout issues.

per_golden_matches.golden_comment: -ms-align-items never existed in any version of IE/Edge; the correct legacy property is -ms-flex-align.
per_golden_matches.matched_candidate: mixins.scss ~118: dead vendor line `-ms-align-items` is not a valid property; old IE syntax is `-ms-flex-align`, so the declaration is silently discarded and provides no IE coverage
per_golden_matches.reasoning: The candidate flags that `-ms-align-items` is not a valid IE/Edge legacy property and explicitly notes the correct property is `-ms-flex-align`, matching the golden issue about the nonexistence of `-ms-align-items` and the proper replacement.

per_golden_matches.golden_comment: -webkit-box-ordinal-group and -moz-box-ordinal-group require values starting from 1, not 0. If $val is 0, this will cause incorrect rendering in older browsers, leading to layout issues.
per_golden_matches.matched_candidate: order mixins: -ms-flex-order/-webkit-box-ordinal-group require integers and default to 1 instead of 0, causing reordering to differ across old/new spec boundaries
per_golden_matches.reasoning: The candidate flags that -webkit-box-ordinal-group (and related legacy order properties) use a 1-based ordinal (defaulting to 1) rather than allowing 0, leading to different ordering/layout behavior in older implementations. This matches the golden issue about needing values starting from 1 and 0 causing incorrect rendering in older browsers.

per_golden_matches.golden_comment: Mixing float: left with flexbox causes layout issues. Further this PR removes the float-based right alignment for .d-header .panel, which may cause the login panel in the non-Ember/noscript header (where .panel is nested inside .row and not a flex item) to stack under the title instead of remaining right-aligned.

adjudication_records.issue_text: header.scss, topic-post.scss, and badges.css.scss use @include flexbox()/align-items/order mixins without importing common/foundation/mixins, which would break the Sass build at asset-compile time

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows new mixins defined in common/foundation/mixins.scss and used via @include in header.scss, topic-post.scss, topic.scss, and badges.css.scss, but it does not show how these SCSS files are bundled/imported. They may already have access to common/foundation/mixins.scss through a higher-level import (e.g., a manifest), so the claim that Sass will break at compile time due to missing imports is not verifiable from this diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Flexbox ordering via order(3) and margin-left: auto fails on -moz-box (Gecko never supported -moz-box-ordinal-group), causing .panel to render left-aligned and header controls to wrap or overlap the title

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds flexbox/ordering mixins and applies `@include flexbox()` to `.contents` and `margin-left: auto` + `@include order(3)` to `.panel`. The finding hinges on a specific claim about Gecko/`-moz-box` support (“Gecko never supported `-moz-box-ordinal-group`”) and predicts concrete misrendering. That browser-compat behavior isn’t verifiable from the diff alone, and the mixin also sets unprefixed `display: flex`/`order`, which modern Gecko would use regardless of any `-moz-box` quirks.

adjudication_records.issue_text: mixins.scss:120 declares display: -moz-inline-box, a fabricated property value never implemented by Gecko, misleading readers into thinking Firefox 2009 inline flex is covered

adjudication.rationale: The diff does add `display: -moz-inline-box;` in `@mixin inline-flex()`, but the finding’s claim that this value is “fabricated” and “never implemented by Gecko” is an external browser-history assertion that cannot be verified from the PR diff itself. The diff alone doesn’t demonstrate broken behavior or reader-misleadingness.

adjudication_records.issue_text: header.scss keeps .valign-helper after .contents became a flex container, leaving a dead-but-styled helper that can shift title vertical alignment and is a hazard for future layout edits

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `.contents` in `header.scss` was changed to a flex container (`@include flexbox(); @include align-items(center);`) and the `.title { float: left; }` rule was removed, but it does not show the definition of `.valign-helper` (only its selector starting) or any markup usage. From the diff alone, we cannot verify that `.valign-helper` is now unused (“dead”) or that it shifts the title’s vertical alignment; it may still be used/needed by the template or have harmless styles.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Flexbox conversion of .contents leaves out-of-diff float/position/width overrides in sibling stylesheets (responsive/mobile rules, plugin/theme overrides) dead or conflicting, breaking mobile/narrow-width header stacking

adjudication.rationale: The diff does convert `.contents` in `header.scss` to flexbox and removes floats on `.title`/`.panel`, but the finding’s core claim depends on *other* “sibling stylesheets (responsive/mobile rules, plugin/theme overrides)” that are not shown in the diff. From this diff alone we cannot verify that any out-of-diff float/position/width overrides exist, become dead/conflicting, or that mobile/narrow-width header stacking is broken.

adjudication_records.issue_text: margin-left: auto push-right technique in the flex mixins fails on 2009 box-model browsers (-webkit-box/-moz-box/-ms-flexbox targets like iOS ≤6, Safari 5, old Android), collapsing the right-aligned header layout

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes the header layout from floats to flex: `.contents` now uses `@include flexbox()` and `.panel` drops `float: right` in favor of `margin-left: auto` plus `@include order(3)`. The new `flexbox()` mixin includes legacy 2009-era syntaxes (`display: -webkit-box; display: -moz-box;`) where `margin-left: auto` is not a reliable/standardized push-right mechanism, so in browsers that pick those modes the right-alignment can fail (regression compared to the prior float-based layout).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Flex conversion of .small-action drops avatar/text spacing with no gap replacement, causing avatar and description text to butt against each other

adjudication.rationale: In `.small-action`, the diff does change layout to flex and reduces `.small-action-desc` spacing (from `padding: ... 4em` + `margin-top: 5px` to `padding: 0 1.5%`), but it does introduce a replacement spacing mechanism (the new padding). The claim that spacing is dropped “with no gap replacement” is not supported by the diff, and the specific visual outcome (“avatar and description text butt against each other”) can’t be verified from the SCSS alone without the corresponding markup/rendering.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Flex conversion of .small-action removes the 4em left padding, misaligning avatar-less small-action variants flush-left with surrounding posts

adjudication.rationale: In `topic-post.scss`, `.small-action-desc` changes from `padding: 0.5em 0 0.5em 4em;` (a fixed 4em left indent) to `padding: 0 1.5%;`, while `.small-action` is converted to flex (`@include flexbox(); @include align-items(center);`). The diff clearly removes the left offset that would keep the description text aligned when there isn’t an avatar consuming space on the left, making a flush-left regression plausible.

adjudication_records.issue_text: -ms-align-items is a nonexistent property (IE10 uses -ms-flex-align), emitting dead declarations and indicating the prefix matrix was never verified

Scope drift: unrelated redesign of .small-action visual styling in topic-post.scss:261-305, rewriting padding/margin scheme of .small-action-desc and zeroing p margins with no connection to header layout performance

adjudication.rationale: The diff does make substantial visual/layout changes to `.small-action` in `topic-post.scss` (adds `@include flexbox()`/`align-items(center)`, changes `.small-action-desc` padding from `0.5em 0 0.5em 4em` + `margin-top: 5px` to `padding: 0 1.5%`, sets nested `p { margin: 0; }`, and removes `padding-top: 4px`). These edits are real and not obviously tied to the header changes shown, so a scope-drift concern is actionable even if the PR intent isn’t provable from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Silent behavioral change masked as refactor: loss of the 4em avatar gutter in .small-action-desc (padding-left: 4em removed) changes rendered position of every small-action description

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly changes `.small-action-desc` from `padding: 0.5em 0 0.5em 4em;` to `padding: 0 1.5%;`, removing the fixed 4em left gutter that likely offset content from the avatar. This is a concrete, user-visible layout change (not a pure refactor), but the diff alone doesn’t prove it’s incorrect/broken—could be intentional alongside the new flexbox alignment.

adjudication_records.issue_text: header.scss:36-39: @include order(3) on .panel plus order(2) on .extra-info-wrapper is a visual reordering feature, not performance optimization, and breaks DOM order = visual order including tab/focus order

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly introduces visual reordering via flexbox: `.panel` gets `@include order(3)` in `header.scss` and `.extra-info-wrapper` gets `@include order(2)` in `topic.scss`, after adding new flexbox/order mixins. Using `order` can cause the visual layout order to differ from DOM order, which can create accessibility/usability issues (e.g., focus/tab order not matching what users see). Whether it definitively breaks tab/focus depends on the HTML/focusable elements, which aren’t shown, but the underlying concern is real and diff-grounded.

adjudication_records.issue_text: mixins.scss:96-131: dead/incorrect legacy prefixes shipped in the diff, including invalid -ms-align-items (never in any spec) and -webkit-box-align/-webkit-box-ordinal-group with modern keyword values invalid under the 2009 box spec

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds new flexbox mixins in `mixins.scss` (lines ~96-131) that include `-ms-align-items`, which is not a valid CSS property and will be ignored by browsers. The mixin also emits legacy 2009-spec properties like `-webkit-box-align` / `-webkit-box-ordinal-group`; while the current call sites pass values like `center`, `baseline`, and small integers (which are likely acceptable), the prefixes are at least questionable/legacy and can become incorrect if modern values (e.g. `flex-start`) are passed later. This is a real, diff-grounded maintainability/compat concern, but not a clearly verifiable functional break introduced by the diff since invalid declarations are simply ignored and valid modern properties are also emitted.

adjudication_records.issue_text: mixins.scss ~118: dead vendor line `-ms-align-items` is not a valid property; old IE syntax is `-ms-flex-align`, so the declaration is silently discarded and provides no IE coverage
matched_golden_ids: -ms-align-items never existed in any version of IE/Edge; the correct legacy property is -ms-flex-align.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate flags that `-ms-align-items` is not a valid IE/Edge legacy property and explicitly notes the correct property is `-ms-flex-align`, matching the golden issue about the nonexistence of `-ms-align-items` and the proper replacement.

adjudication_records.issue_text: mixins.scss align-items/order mixins pass modern flexbox values verbatim into 2009-spec properties without value translation (e.g. flex-start is invalid for -webkit-box-align/-ms-flex-align), causing silent layout breakage in legacy browsers

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `@mixin align-items($alignment)` and `@mixin order($val)` that write legacy 2009 flexbox properties (`-webkit-box-align`, `-webkit-box-ordinal-group`, `-moz-box-*`) using the same values as modern flexbox. Those legacy properties require different value forms/indexing (e.g., `-webkit-box-align` expects `start/end/center/baseline/stretch`, not `flex-start/flex-end`; `-webkit-box-ordinal-group` is 1-based whereas modern `order` is 0-based). This can produce invalid/ineffective CSS and thus broken layout in legacy implementations, which is exactly what the finding describes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: order mixins: -ms-flex-order/-webkit-box-ordinal-group require integers and default to 1 instead of 0, causing reordering to differ across old/new spec boundaries
matched_golden_ids: -webkit-box-ordinal-group and -moz-box-ordinal-group require values starting from 1, not 0. If $val is 0, this will cause incorrect rendering in older browsers, leading to layout issues.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate flags that -webkit-box-ordinal-group (and related legacy order properties) use a 1-based ordinal (defaulting to 1) rather than allowing 0, leading to different ordering/layout behavior in older implementations. This matches the golden issue about needing values starting from 1 and 0 causing incorrect rendering in older browsers.

adjudication_records.issue_text: topic.scss:30 / header.scss:~40: visual reordering via order(2)/order(3) diverges from DOM order, breaking keyboard focus and tab order (WCAG 1.3.2 / 2.4.3 violation)

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces flexbox-based visual reordering via `@include order(2)` in `topic.scss` (`.extra-info-wrapper`) and `@include order(3)` in `header.scss` (`.panel`), enabled by making `.contents` a flex container. Using CSS `order` can cause the visual reading order to diverge from DOM order, which is an accessibility concern (tab/focus order follows DOM). The diff shows the mechanism that could create this mismatch, though the PR diff alone doesn’t prove that focusable elements are actually reordered in a way that violates WCAG in the rendered UI.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Silent visual redesign of .small-action in topic-post.scss:277-291 — padding/margin changes alter spacing of all small-action blocks unrelated to PR's stated header performance objective; the 1.5% width-dependent padding is a new visual decision rather than mechanical flex conversion

adjudication.rationale: The diff in `topic-post.scss` changes `.small-action` layout and spacing beyond a pure “flex conversion”: it adds `@include flexbox()` / `@include align-items(center)` and replaces `.small-action-desc` padding/margin (`padding: 0.5em 0 0.5em 4em; margin-top: 5px;`) with `padding: 0 1.5%`, plus resets nested `p` margins and removes `padding-top: 4px`. These are concrete, potentially wide-reaching visual/layout changes to all `.small-action` blocks, so the concern about an unintended/undeclared redesign is diff-grounded (though whether it conflicts with the PR objective can’t be verified from the diff alone).

adjudication_records.issue_text: topic.scss:27-33 — deletion of &.bullet { margin-top: 5px } and addition of line-height: 1.5 to .extra-info-wrapper are unverified visual changes that shift category bullet badges vertically on every instance

adjudication.rationale: The diff does remove `.badge-wrapper { &.bullet { margin-top: 5px; } }` inside `.extra-info-wrapper` and adds `line-height: 1.5` to `.extra-info-wrapper` (topic.scss). Those are real CSS changes that can affect vertical alignment/spacing of bullet-style category badges, so it’s reasonable to flag as a visual-regression risk to verify. However, the claim that it will shift badges vertically “on every instance” isn’t strictly verifiable from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: mixins.scss:117 — align-items mixin emits nonexistent -ms-align-items property, producing dead declarations in every compiled stylesheet using it and misleading future maintainers debugging legacy flex alignment

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds an `@mixin align-items($alignment)` in `mixins.scss` that emits both `-ms-flex-align: $alignment;` and `-ms-align-items: $alignment;`. The presence of `-ms-align-items` is verifiable in the added mixin and is not a standard/recognized legacy flexbox property (unlike `-ms-flex-align`), so it will compile to a no-op/dead declaration. This is a maintainability/clarity issue rather than a functional defect visible from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: align-items mixin family is internally inconsistent: -moz-box equivalent for align-items is missing while -moz-box-ordinal-group is included in order()

adjudication.rationale: In mixins.scss, the new `flexbox()` mixin sets `display: -moz-box;`, but the new `align-items($alignment)` mixin does not include the corresponding legacy property (`-moz-box-align`). Meanwhile `order($val)` does include `-moz-box-ordinal-group`. This is an internal inconsistency in the vendor-prefix support added by this diff and would prevent alignment from working in environments that actually use `-moz-box`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: PR description mismatch: the diff is a layout-mechanism rewrite with visual re-spacing, not the stated performance optimization, so commit history records a false reason for user-visible changes and will mislead regression bisecting

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly changes layout/styling (floats to flexbox, spacing tweaks, new flexbox mixins), but the finding hinges on a mismatch with the PR description/intent (“stated performance optimization”), which is not present in the diff. From the diff alone, we cannot verify what the PR claimed or whether commit history records a false reason.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The `order` mixin omits `-moz-box-ordinal-group`, so header panel reordering silently does nothing on old-Firebox flexbox engine the mixin targets, causing the panel to sit adjacent to the title instead of right-aligned

adjudication.rationale: The finding claims the `order` mixin omits `-moz-box-ordinal-group`, but the diff explicitly adds it in `app/assets/stylesheets/common/foundation/mixins.scss` under `@mixin order($val) { ... -moz-box-ordinal-group: $val; ... }`. Therefore the stated browser-compat reordering failure is not supported by the changes shown.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The mixin is internally inconsistent: it emits `-moz-box` compat lines for Firefox 18-21 but `order()` doesn't support that engine — either the compat targets are real (and broken) or the dead `-moz-box` lines should be deleted

adjudication.rationale: The diff’s `order($val)` mixin *does* emit a `-moz` declaration intended for the legacy `-moz-box` model (`-moz-box-ordinal-group: $val;`), so the specific claim that the mixin targets `-moz-box` but `order()` “doesn't support that engine” is not supported by the code shown. The proposed inconsistency is not verifiable as stated from this diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The `-ms-align-items` declaration in `align-items()` is not a real property (IE10 uses `-ms-flex-align`), making it a redundant dead declaration

adjudication.rationale: In `app/assets/stylesheets/common/foundation/mixins.scss`, the new `@mixin align-items($alignment)` includes both `-ms-flex-align: $alignment;` and `-ms-align-items: $alignment;`. The latter is not a standard/commonly supported MS prefixed property for flexbox alignment (IE10 uses `-ms-flex-align`), so it is effectively a dead/redundant declaration. This is cleanup/compatibility correctness rather than a functional defect shown by the diff.
